grammar.title: Passive Reporting Structures (It is said that..., He is thought to...)
grammar.explanation:
In news and formal writing, we often report what people in general say, think, or believe without naming anyone. Instead of saying who said it, we use a passive reporting structure, and this keeps the tone formal and distant, even a little aloof.

There are two main patterns. The first is **It + passive + that clause**, as in **It is said that** he is rich. The second is **subject + passive + to-infinitive**, as in He **is said to be** rich. Never mix the two patterns.

Common reporting verbs include **say**, **think**, **believe**, **know**, **report**, **expect**, **consider**, **claim**, **allege**, **estimate**, and **suspect**. A speaker who has an aversion to naming sources will favour these forms, since they hide the source completely.

Choose the infinitive by time. Use **to + verb** for the same time or a general fact, **to be + -ing** for something in progress now, **to have + past participle** for an earlier action, and **to have been + -ing** for an earlier action in progress.

The reporting verb itself can be past, as in She **was reported to have left** the hospital. With **there**, match the verb to the noun: There **are said to be** many problems, never there is said to be many problems.
examples: ***It is said that** the castle is haunted.* (It + that clause)
*The castle **is said to be** haunted.* (subject + to-infinitive)
***It is expected that** prices will rise.* (expect)
*The new bridge **is expected to open** in 2028.* (future)
*The singer **is reported to be recording** a new album.* (in progress)

practice.q: Rewrite with a passive reporting structure: People say that she is blissfully happy in her new job.
practice.a: It is said that she is blissfully happy in her new job. / She is said to be blissfully happy in her new job.

practice.q: Rewrite with a passive reporting structure: People believe that he left the party early because he felt aloof.
practice.a: He is believed to have left the party early because he felt aloof.

practice.q: Rewrite with a passive reporting structure: People report that the singer is recording a new album at the moment.
practice.a: The singer is reported to be recording a new album at the moment.

practice.q: Rewrite with a passive reporting structure: People think that she has an aversion to public speaking.
practice.a: She is thought to have an aversion to public speaking. / It is thought that she has an aversion to public speaking.
